1.explanation:
1. src/field/index.js: shows the exact code (line 35) where the passed-in values are assigned by reference.
2. field/index.en-us.md & field/index.md: document the Field component’s API, including the values prop and how it’s expected to be used.
3. field/demo/basic.md: demonstrates passing a values prop into Field, reproducing the basic scenario where the incoming object is stored.
4. field/demo/normalize.md: shows how normalization logic can mutate values, highlighting unintended side effects when values is not cloned.
5. field/demo/onchange.md: illustrates how onChange updates Field.values, which in the current implementation would also alter the original object.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows the Field component’s constructor (src/field/index.js line 35) doing “this.values = options.values || {}”. Because it takes a direct reference to the passed-in values object, any updates the Field class makes to this.values will also mutate the original data the caller supplied. The bug is that Field is modifying incoming data instead of cloning it first, so callers cannot preserve immutability of their values prop.
